context: Tests whether the agent's written design advisory (design.md) applies the documented Go decision rules: interfaces defined at the consumer, small and discovered not invented, constructors that accept interfaces and return concrete types, goroutines with bounded lifetimes driven by context cancellation and errgroup-style waiting, context as the first parameter of blocking calls, %w error wrapping with lowercase punctuation-free messages, and explicit trade-off statements. The fixture deliberately dangles a fat seven-method producer-side interface proposal as the tempting answer.

checklist.name: Advisory artifact written
checklist.description: design.md exists in the repository root and addresses both the interface decision and the FlushLoop design.

checklist.name: Interface belongs to the consumer
checklist.description: The advisory recommends defining the ledger interface in the consuming package (internal/audit), not in the producer package (internal/ledger) as TEAM_NOTES.md proposed.

checklist.name: Fat interface rejected
checklist.description: The advisory explicitly identifies the seven-method LedgerStore proposal as an invented abstraction and advises against defining all seven methods up front; the interface should be discovered from what the audit package actually uses.

checklist.name: Interface is small and focused
checklist.description: The proposed interface contains only the method(s) the audit flusher needs (AppendEntries, or AppendEntries plus at most one other), not the full ledger surface.

checklist.name: Constructor accepts interface, returns concrete
checklist.description: The advisory shows or states that Collector (or its constructor) should accept the small interface as a parameter while returning the concrete *Collector type, not an interface.

checklist.name: Flush loop uses context cancellation
checklist.description: The flush-loop design exits via context cancellation (select on ctx.Done alongside the queue drain), not via time.Sleep polling, an ignore channel, or an unbounded for loop.

checklist.name: Goroutine lifetime is bounded and stated
checklist.description: The advisory states explicitly when the flush goroutine exits and who knows when it is done (e.g. errgroup g.Wait or a WaitGroup waited on by the caller / graceful-shutdown path).

checklist.name: Context is first parameter of blocking calls
checklist.description: In the proposed design or snippets, blocking calls (queue drain, ledger writes, shutdown wait) take context.Context as their first parameter; FlushLoop without a context is flagged as needing one.

checklist.name: Error handling in snippets follows the wrapping rules
checklist.description: Any error handling shown wraps with %w and lowercase messages without trailing punctuation; no %v wrapping that breaks the chain for wrapped internal errors, and no log-and-return of the same error.

checklist.name: Trade-offs stated with a choice
checklist.description: The advisory names the alternatives considered (e.g. interface location, batching vs single writes, tick-based vs drain-on-signal) and states which it would choose and why, not just a list of options.

checklist.name: Leads with code
checklist.description: design.md contains at least one Go code snippet making a non-obvious recommendation concrete (the interface definition and/or the flush loop).
